title: Arriving in Kansas City: the Booker T Hotel and Piney Brown
summary: Saunders lived at 18th and Vine, just before the Cherry Blossom opened, with Basie and others struggling; Piney Brown was a notable pimp three doors away.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: -- hustling to this. This was a great -- and when I played Kansas City, this was a great -- see, we got a chance to move around, and when I went to Kansas City, Basie and them were starving. Basie, George [E. Lee].

Well, they were -- we were all hanging out -- right, no, this was just before the Orange Blossom, just before. We were living at 18th and Vine, then. It was a hotel there, and the guys used to just hang out there, and, man, all the musicians in the world, they all loved each other, though.
Was there such a person as Piney Brown?
Oh, yeah, he was one of the biggest pimps. Piney Brown, he was one of the biggest pimps. I lived
about three doors from him in the hotel.
On the same floor. Right, right, Piney Brown.
